rawCommits.subject: fix(projects): show Standard Agent immediately + block double-add
rawCommits.body:

synchronous `activatingRef` inside the list now short-circuits the
second activation; an effect releases it when `creating` settles back
to `null` (success, error, or modal close all hit the upstream

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-stream): make Stop actually abort the in-flight SSE
rawCommits.body:
The per-partition send-control refactor (c7761524d) moved the
AbortController that performSend hands to `api.sendEventStream` off
`streamMetaMap[key].abort` and onto
`partitionSendControlMap[key].currentController`. `stopStreaming`
still only routed through `core.baseStopStreaming()`, which aborts
the former — the chat path's controller was never touched, so
pressing Stop did nothing: the SSE reader kept running, deltas
kept arriving, and the UI never flipped out of "streaming".

Abort `ctrl.currentController` (and null it) in `stopStreaming`
before falling through to `baseStopStreaming`. The agent-chat /
task-stream paths still use the legacy abort slot, so leave
`baseStopStreaming`'s behavior intact.

Regression test in parallel-chats.test.ts captures the AbortSignal
handed to `api.sendEventStream`, calls `stopStreaming`, and asserts
the signal flips to `aborted` and the partition's controller is
cleared.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-stream): keep cooking shimmer pinned for the entire active turn
rawCommits.body:
The pinned phase indicator above the chat input was popping in and out
mid-turn because `getStreamingPhaseLabel` returned `null` whenever
`isWriting` was true (word-by-word reveal in progress). `isWriting`
oscillates true -> false -> true on every reveal step, so the shimmer
unmounted and remounted continuously instead of staying live for the
full turn. The visibility gate is already correctly defined upstream by
`nowStreaming` (true while `isStreaming`, streamed text, thinking
buffer, or tool calls are active) and cleared by `finalizeStream` /
`AssistantMessageEnd`, so we no longer need the `isWriting` short
circuit.

- Drop the `isWriting` early-return in `getStreamingPhaseLabel` and the
  `progressText === "queued"` -> null branch; the queued state now
  surfaces as a stable "Queued..." shimmer so the pinned slot continues
  to represent the active turn.
- Stop selecting / forwarding `isWriting` from `ChatStreamingIndicator`
  and drop the `hidden` prop on `CookingIndicator` (label is always
  non-null on the active path).
- Remove the duplicate input-bar queued pill: `ChatPanel` no longer
  derives or forwards `isQueued`, since the pinned shimmer is now the
  single source of truth for "turn in progress" including the queued
  state.
- Update unit tests: the writing-flag case now asserts the shimmer
  stays mounted, and a new case asserts the "Queued..." label.

rawCommits.subject: fix(protocol): wire Phase 6 Progress variant + first-class support_id
rawCommits.body:
Lands the aura-os side of the Phase 6 harness changes so the
workspace compiles again after the new OutboundMessage::Progress
variant from aura-protocol/server.rs reached the server's
exhaustive match in persist_task_dispatch::handle_outbound.

Changes:
- aura-protocol: add Progress(ProgressMsg) variant + promote
  support_id to a first-class optional field on ErrorMsg
  (#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
  keeps the wire backwards compatible in both directions).
- aura-os-server: add the missing Progress(_) match arm to
  is_persistable_outbound (returns false - heartbeats forward
  to SSE but aren't persisted as SessionEvents and don't bump the
  throttled progress publish since they ARE the progress publish).
- aura-os-server::errors: when a remapped harness ErrorMsg
  arrives with a pre-stamped support_id (Phase 6 in-process emit
  sites pre-populate the field), reuse that id instead of minting
  a fresh one so a single error never carries two different ids
  across surfaces. Skip double-suffixing on retries.
- aura-os-harness::ws_bridge + every server-side ErrorMsg
  construction site: pass support_id: None so older emit sites
  still compile.

Without this commit the entire server crate fails to build with
error[E0004] on the non-exhaustive match.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-input): keep wrapped prompt in multi-line layout on backspace
rawCommits.body:
The multi-line detector measured the textarea's `scrollHeight` at the
current layout, but the multi-line state itself widens the textarea (the
inline-picker `padding-right: min(220px, 42%)` reservation gets dropped).
That widening made the same wrapping prompt fit on a single line at the
new width, so the very next keystroke flipped the detector back to
single-line, slid the picker back inline, narrowed the textarea, and
re-wrapped the text — a per-character oscillation that meant backspace
inside a still-wrapping prompt visibly snapped the layout back to one
line.

Two fixes:

1. Anti-oscillation: when we're already in multi-line and the natural
   measurement says single-line, re-measure with the inline-picker
   padding-right reserved and only collapse when the prompt would also
   fit on one line at that narrower width. The expression is wrapped
   in `calc(...)` so JSDOM's CSSOM accepts it for the regression test
   (real browsers parse both forms identically).

2. Width-aware re-measure: a `ResizeObserver` on the textarea fires
   `autoResize()` whenever the layout swap actually changes the
   textarea's width (and on JSDOM where ResizeObserver is undefined,
   the effect quietly no-ops). This keeps the inline `height` we set
   and the multi-line flag coherent with the post-swap layout — without
   it the textarea could be left taller than its current content after
   the picker drops to the footer.

Adds a regression test that stubs `scrollHeight` to mirror the
"narrow wraps, wide fits" behavior and asserts the picker stays in
the bottom row across a backspace.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat-error-row): inline error message with Support ID + Report Bug
rawCommits.body:
The Support ID + Report Bug action row was correctly gated to error
turns only, but the error string was concatenated into the bubble's
`content` (often as `*Error: ...*`), so the chip and the message it
referred to ended up stacked on separate lines with no visual link
between them. Split the error string off `content` into a dedicated
`errorMessage` field on `DisplaySessionEvent`, and render it as the
leading element of `errorActionsRow` -- truncated to a single line
with the full text exposed via `title` on hover.

Side-effects of the split: `content` now carries only the partial
streaming buffer captured before the turn errored, so the buffered
prose still renders through `LLMOutput` unchanged; the streamDropped
banner keeps its title but drops the duplicate message span; the
insufficient-credits "Buy credits" button moves into the action row
so the whole error chrome reads as one line.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): anchor rustc parity parser so rustup 1.29 banner stops failing macos-latest
rawCommits.body:
`scripts/ci/check-runtime.mjs desktop` was failing every macos-latest
aarch64 nightly with `found rustc 1.29.0` even though
`dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.94.1` and `rust-toolchain.toml` correctly
install Rust 1.94.1. Root cause: `parseVersion` greedily matched the
first `\d+.\d+.\d+` in the combined stdout+stderr from `rustc --version`,
and the macos-latest image now ships rustup 1.29.0 (released 2026-03-12),
whose proxy emits info lines mentioning its own `1.29.0` before stdout's
`rustc 1.94.1` ever shows up.

Anchor the parse to the literal program name (`rustc 1.94.1 (...)`) and
include the raw capture in the failure message so the next stray version
banner is debuggable straight from the CI log.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: anchor rustc parity parser so rustup 1.29 banner stops failing macos-latest

rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): resolve rustc via `rustup which` so Homebrew's rustup-init shim stops failing macos-latest
rawCommits.body:
Yesterday's anchor-the-regex fix was the right idea on the wrong layer:
the parity check is still failing on macos-latest aarch64 because
`rustc --version` literally prints

  rustup-init 1.29.0 (2026-03-05)

The macos-latest GitHub runner ships Homebrew's `rustup` formula, which
installs `/opt/homebrew/bin/rustc` as a symlink to `rustup-init` and puts
`/opt/homebrew/bin` ahead of `~/.cargo/bin` on PATH. Invoked under the
name `rustc`, that `rustup-init` binary does not dispatch as a proxy --
it just prints its own identity. No amount of regex hardening can recover
a rustc version from output that doesn't contain one.

Fix: resolve the rustc binary up front via `rustup which rustc`, which
returns the toolchain-managed path (e.g.
`/Users/runner/.rustup/toolchains/1.94.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/rustc`)
regardless of what `rustc` on PATH would have hit. Add a `tryCapture`
helper for non-fatal probes, and gate the parsed output on a real
`rustc X.Y.Z` line so a future shim regression fails with a targeted,
actionable error instead of a misleading `found rustc 1.29.0`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: resolve rustc via `rustup which` so Homebrew's rustup-init shim stops failing macos-latest

rawCommits.subject: chore(ci): re-run desktop nightly to validate macos-latest rustc + harness sync
rawCommits.body:
Re-trigger Desktop Nightly Release after two unblockers landed:

  1. 6210a72b5 fix(ci): resolve rustc via `rustup which` so Homebrew's
     rustup-init shim stops failing macos-latest. The macos-latest arm64
     runner was reporting `rustc 1.29.0` because PATH resolved `rustc`
     to `/opt/homebrew/bin/rustup-init`, which doesn't dispatch as a
     proxy. The check now goes through `rustup which rustc`.

  2. cypher-asi/aura-harness@c394e04 (fast-forwarded onto main from
     fix/agent-stuck-and-reset). Lands the matching `ErrorMsg.support_id`
     and `SessionUsage.context_breakdown` field initializers in
     `aura-runtime`, so the sidecar build no longer hits 19 E0063
     "missing field" errors against the new aura-protocol schema.

This commit is intentionally empty -- nothing to ship in aura-os itself,
just a fresh push event to re-enter the workflow with both fixes in place.

rendered.title: Video generation in chat, stuck-stream recovery, and a refreshed input bar
rendered.intro: A heavy nightly that lands native video generation inside chat, ships an end-to-end "agent stuck and silent drops" recovery story (watchdogs, queued sends, support IDs, one-click bug reports), and reorganizes the chat input bar around an inline model picker and a richer per-bucket context indicator. Desktop release infrastructure also got unblocked on macOS-latest after a rustup shim regression.

entries.title: Video generation joins chat, and stuck streams stop swallowing messages
entries.summary: A large morning push that introduces video as a first-class chat mode end to end and lands the core of the agent-stuck/silent-drops recovery work across client and server.

items.text: Video becomes a first-class chat generation mode: a new VideoBlock renders inline HTML5 playback (with a 0.5s poster frame and MP4 download), the agent mode system, slash command, model picker, progress text, and queue/dispatch paths all learn the video case, and the standalone-agent stream no longer misroutes video into image/3D rendering.

AURA Video gains Seedance 2.0 and 2.0 Fast alongside Veo, with provider-aware resolution, duration, and aspect-ratio constraints; Seedance ships visible but disabled with a "coming soon" label until the BytePlus account is live.

Video and 3D generation turns now persist into chat history: server handlers resolve the agent/session context and call the standard persist pipeline, and the frontend passes agentId/agentInstanceId through both project and standalone agent flows.

Stuck-stream recovery lands across the chat surface: a 30s SSE-idle watchdog flips the cooking indicator into a StuckStreamPill with Stop/Retry, a 60s auto-timeout finalizes the stream with a synthetic transcript event, and messages typed during an in-flight turn are now queued instead of silently dropped. Stop also actually aborts the in-flight SSE on the project-chat partition path.

Server tightens hang detection and adds traceability: first-event timeout drops 120s→90s and max-idle 30min→3min, a tool-heartbeat env knob is added, and every SSE-bound ErrorMsg is now stamped with a short support_id and logged via structured tracing so user reports join cleanly to server logs.

Reset actually resets standalone agent chats: a new GET /api/agents/:agent_id/sessions/:session_id/events endpoint scopes history to the pinned session so pressing "+" or RotateCcw no longer drags prior-session messages back in, and the message queue is cleared on new-chat to prevent leaked sends.

Project agent picker stops hiding the Standard Agent row behind a network spinner and guards against fast double-clicks creating duplicate instances, and the Chat app's "+" now opens the same AgentSelectorModal scoped to CEO Home so users stay inside the Chat app instead of jumping to /projects.

Chat input bar gains a Cursor-style Context popover with per-bucket token counts (System prompt / Tools / Skills / MCP / Subagents / Conversation), powered by a new context_breakdown field on SessionUsage emitted from the harness.
Small polish: the EARN credits pill label is optically recentered.

entries.title: One-click Report Bug, progress-ring context pill, and a tidier input bar
entries.summary: A follow-up wave that turns the stuck-stream and support_id plumbing into a real bug-reporting flow and reshuffles the chat input bar so context and model controls finally read as one row.

items.text: Report Bug becomes one click: a 50-entry breadcrumb ring buffer plus support_id parsing now feed a new ReportBugButton that opens the existing feedback modal pre-filled with build version, stream key, agent/session ids, the last 3 support_ids, and the last 20 breadcrumbs — wired into the chat error bubble and the StuckStreamPill, replacing the Phase-2 console.warn placeholder.

The context pill becomes a small SVG progress ring + lowercase "NN% context" chip with warning (≥70%) and danger (≥90%) color states, and is re-aligned to share the exact box model as the neighbouring project and model buttons.

Desktop chat input reorganizes: the model picker moves inline next to the send button so the active model is visible alongside the typing target, leaving the context indicator alone at the far right of the bottom info bar.

The pinned cooking shimmer now stays mounted for the entire active turn (including a stable "Queued…" state) instead of flickering on every word-by-word reveal step, and the redundant inline reset-context button is removed in favor of the single "+" new-chat affordance.

entries.title: Protocol catch-up for Phase 6 progress events and first-class support_id
entries.summary: A targeted server/protocol change that re-syncs aura-os with the Phase 6 harness so the workspace builds and support IDs survive end-to-end.

items.text: aura-protocol gains an OutboundMessage::Progress variant for harness heartbeats and promotes support_id to a first-class optional field on ErrorMsg (kept wire-backwards-compatible via skip_serializing_if). The server handles the new variant in its exhaustive match, and the error remapper reuses a pre-stamped support_id instead of minting a second one — so a single error never carries two different IDs across surfaces.

entries.title: Multi-line input bar reflow and richer agent-chat context wiring
entries.summary: Afternoon polish on the input bar's layout when prompts wrap, plus restoring the per-bucket context view on the standalone agent surfaces.

items.text: When the chat textarea wraps to a second row, the model picker now drops into a new bottom-left footer slot inside the input container so long prompts get full width, with the +/send buttons re-anchored to share a baseline with the picker. A ResizeObserver + padding-aware re-measure prevents the picker from oscillating in and out of the footer on each keystroke when backspacing inside a still-wrapping prompt.

The rich per-bucket Context popover now works on the Chat-app and standalone agent surfaces too: usage.context_breakdown is parsed via a shared snake→camel helper, and mid-turn TextDelta / ThinkingDelta / ToolResult bumps make the context ring move live instead of jumping only at turn boundaries.

Picking Standard Agent from the Chat app's "+" modal now hydrates the new agent into the store via api.agents.get before navigating, so the destination route renders the new chat immediately instead of silently falling back to the CEO agent.
The sliding-pill animation on the chat mode selector is restored, and the spec block hoists its Copy button into the header's trailing slot to free vertical space.

entries.title: Error bubbles read as one line with their Support ID and Report Bug action
entries.summary: The chat error chrome is reorganized so the error message, support_id chip, and primary action live on a single row.

items.text: Error messages are split off the bubble's content into a dedicated errorMessage field and rendered as the leading element of the error actions row — truncated to one line with full text on hover — so the Support ID chip and the Report Bug button finally sit next to the message they describe. The insufficient-credits "Buy credits" button also moves into the same row so the whole error chrome reads as one line.

entries.title: macOS-latest nightly unblocked after a rustup-init shim regression
entries.summary: Desktop nightly was failing on the macos-latest arm64 runner because Homebrew's rustup-init was masquerading as rustc; the runtime parity check now resolves the real toolchain binary.

items.text: The desktop runtime parity check stopped trusting `rustc --version` output verbatim — first by anchoring the parser to a literal `rustc X.Y.Z` line, then by resolving rustc up front via `rustup which rustc` so Homebrew's `/opt/homebrew/bin/rustc` symlink to rustup-init can no longer report itself as "rustc 1.29.0" on macos-latest. A fresh empty commit re-triggers the Desktop Nightly Release workflow with the fix plus the matching aura-harness sync in place.

highlights: Video generation lands as a first-class chat mode with Veo + Seedance
Stuck-stream watchdog, queued sends, and Report Bug with support IDs
Per-bucket Context popover and inline model picker in the chat input
macOS-latest nightly unblocked after rustup-init shim regression
